title: Hybrid cohort eviction verifier and correctness guarantees for KV cache under continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define, implement, and verify a hybrid eviction policy that combines LRU, TTL, and prefix-aware cohort constraints for Redwood's GPU KV cache. The goal is to guarantee correctness invariants (no use-after-evict, deterministic prefix isolation, atomic pin/unpin) while preserving throughput under continuous batching and minimizing GPU memory fragmentation.
background: Current eviction efforts focus on heuristics (LRU, TTL) and prefix-aware heuristics in isolation. Production workloads that use continuous batching and long-lived conversation prefixes expose subtle races: inflight batches may read KV state while concurrent evictions (or demotions to host memory) happen, leading to correctness edge cases, increased latency, and N+1 prefetch storms. Existing tickets cover eviction performance and TTL semantics separately, but we lack a single verified policy and an automated verifier + chaos harness that proves invariants under concurrent batching and lease/cohort semantics.
proposed_solution: Introduce a hybrid eviction controller with: 1) prefix cohorts that establish eviction fences per customer/prefix group; 2) lease-based pinning for inflight batches with fast-path pin/unpin; 3) dual watermarks (soft and hard) integrating LRU score and TTL age; 4) demotion path to pinned GPU slab -> host page with atomic pointer swap; 5) a lightweight formal model (TLA+/Promela sketch) of the key operations, and 6) a chaos verifier that runs synthetic continuous-batching traces against an instrumented runtime to validate invariants.
acceptance_criteria: Formal model expresses and checks the three core invariants: (a) NoReadAfterEvict: a request can never observe a KV entry after it has been evicted without seeing a coherent replacement; (b) PrefixIsolation: eviction of entries from cohort A cannot invalidate entries still pinned by cohort B; (c) AtomicPinUnpin: pin/unpin is linearizable for inflight batches.
Automated verifier (model checker or bounded model) reproduces at least 5 classes of known races and marks them resolved under the new protocol.
Chaos harness (containerized) runs 24h synthetic continuous-batching workload with mixed sequence lengths and shows zero correctness violations across 1000 test runs.
No perf regression >5% median latency at p50/p90 under representative workload (compare to baseline runtime-1.18).
GPU memory fragmentation metric improves or remains stable vs baseline; demotion path does not increase host-to-GPU thrash above 10% of token cost.
Comprehensive unit + integration test coverage added; PR landed and merged; rollout staged with canary and rollback plan.
Documentation updated (design doc + operational runbook) and a post-mortem template for future eviction incidents added to Confluence.
tasks: Write high-level design doc: cohort definitions, watermarks, and demotion contract
Produce formal model sketch (TLA+ or Promela) capturing pin/unpin, evict, demote, and read semantics
Implement eviction controller: hybrid scorer, cohort manager, and lease pin fast-path
Add atomic demotion mechanism: slab pointer swap and host-side tombstones
Extend telemetry: eviction decisions, pin/unpin latency, demotion counts, fragmentation histogram
Build chaos verifier harness that exercises continuous batching with interleaved evict/demote operations
Write unit tests around race windows and fuzz eviction boundaries
Run performance benchmarks and iterate on heuristic weights
Create rollout plan: internal canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full, with auto-fallback to bounded-LRU policy
Author docs and runbook; schedule brown-bag for SRE/Platform engineers
testing_plan: Unit tests assert invariants in single-threaded and mocked concurrent contexts. Integration tests run against a local multi-worker runtime with synthetic prefix cohorts. Chaos verifier injects delays, GPU OOM signals, demotion slowdowns, and network partition of host backing store. Bounded model checking will target small-state models (3 cohorts, 2 inflight batches each) and enumerate interleavings. Performance bench harness compares end-to-end request latency / tokens/sec to baseline across three workload profiles (short chat, medium multi-turn, long instru prompts).
risks: Added complexity in eviction controller risks regressions and rollout churn
Demotion to host memory can introduce tail latency if host hot-swap isn't optimized
Formal model may under-approximate real system due to unmodeled optimizations (kernel-level batching)
Heuristic tuning for hybrid score may require multiple production iterations
mitigations: Ship behind feature flag with strict canary gating and automatic fallback
Limit demotion rate initially and use admission controller to cap host-to-gpu migrations
Collaborate with runtime and kernel teams to add tracing hooks that align model events with runtime telemetry
Keep the initial implementation conservative: prefer correctness over aggressive memory reclamation
notes: Model artifacts to be stored in repo: infra/eviction-verifier/tla/ and infra/eviction-verifier/harness/
Prototype experiments should be run on a dedicated dev fleet node to avoid interfering with production quotas
